video.title: Facebook Ads For Beginners: Complete Guide (2026)

summary: Chris Koerner presents a beginner’s guide to Facebook Ads Manager, covering campaign setup, ad copy and creative, testing, retargeting, scaling, and lead follow-up. He uses local services such as tree trimming and HVAC repair to illustrate how businesses can attract and handle leads. The video gives many practical benchmarks and sample budgets, but most business results are examples or rules of thumb rather than verified case studies. Its closing shortcuts include competitor research, customer testimonials, and testing an offer before building the product.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; presents the guide.

unit_economics_claims: The host says a home-service ad generated leads for under $5; the Thumbtack comparison is over $50 per lead.
A sample tree-trimming side-hustle scenario says a $5 daily ad budget booked four jobs in the first week, then scales to $40 a day and two crews.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; sample ad budgets are described in metric_claims.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: A sample lead-generation section says a first lead may arrive within one to two days; first paid job timing is not stated.

acquisition.how: Paid social campaigns can be set up and monitored with software, and inbound leads can arrive automatically; creative and optimization still need routine human checks.

onboarding.how: An instant reply and a lead tracker can capture details, but the business must confirm scope, address and scheduling.

delivery.how: Tree work, cleanup and hauling require people and physical equipment on site.

billing.how: Invoicing and payment collection could use software, but the transcript does not describe a billing process.

support.how: Templates and instant replies can handle routine questions, but estimates, safety questions and job changes need human attention.

uk_applicability.notes: Local service ads and tree work can operate in the UK, with changes for local pricing, insurance, safety requirements and service areas. Inbound paid ads are a suitable acquisition channel.

risks: The transcript does not address insurance, safe tree work, equipment costs, weather or job-level margins.
The lead-cost example does not establish that jobs were profitable.

tactics.name: Match objective to customer action
steps: Choose Messages when the goal is an inbox conversation.
Choose Leads to collect names and emails.
Choose Sales or conversions for website purchases.
Choose video views only when video views are the intended outcome.

quote.text: if you want messages in your inbox you choose messages if you want to collect names and emails you choose leads
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Write a specific local-service offer
steps: Name the painful problem the customer has now.
Describe the specific service and a time frame.
Make the next action clear, such as messaging for a free quote.
Use proof or concrete expectations where available.

quote.text: you want a clear solution to a painful problem with a timeline and a path to action
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Build the campaign in Ads Manager
steps: Use Meta Ads Manager rather than boosting a post.
Name the campaign with service, objective and date.
Set the objective, audience, placements and daily budget at the campaign and ad-set levels.
Use a single image or video, then write primary text, a short headline and an appropriate call to action.
Review the offer and creative before publishing.

quote.text: always use Meta Ads Manager it gives you full control
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Start with broad local targeting
steps: Set the service area around the current city.
Start broad and let the platform optimize before adding interests.
Use manual placements if you want to limit where ads appear.
Compare feed and story placements only after an ad has shown results.

quote.text: you want to start broad let the algorithm work dial it in as you go
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a four-part ad-copy framework
steps: Open with a hook tied to a problem or curiosity.
Show the customer that you understand the problem.
Explain the offer with specifics and a time frame.
Tell the reader exactly what to do next.

quote.text: the hook the problem the offer the call to action so let's break it all down
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Wait before changing a new ad
steps: Let a newly published ad run for 72 hours unless it is rejected or clearly broken.
Change one variable at a time so the result is interpretable.
Use the observed result to decide what to change next.

quote.text: do not touch your ad for 72 hours unless it's completely broken like the wrong photo a typo or it's rejected
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test one variable at a time
steps: Start with the image or video.
Then test the primary text and hook.
Next test the headline, audience and placement.
Keep budget even between variants, then retain the winner and stop the loser.

quote.text: only test one variable at a time that's it one thing don't pull more than one lever at a time
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Troubleshoot based on where the funnel stalls
steps: If people do not click, improve the image or hook.
If they click but do not message, clarify the offer and call to action.
If they message but do not book, respond faster and provide clear next steps.
If clicks are expensive, try broader targeting or a different image.

quote.text: if people are messaging and you're not closing these deals then you got to improve your speed to respond
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Retarget engaged prospects
steps: Create a second ad for people who interacted with the original ad or visited the site but did not convert.
Use a more personal reminder and a clear next action.
Keep the retargeting budget low and let the ad run in the background.

quote.text: this one is for warm traffic people who saw your ad or visited your site but never converted
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Scale after repeatable results
steps: Wait for consistent leads and actual customers before scaling.
Increase the budget gradually, checking that performance holds.
Alternatively, duplicate a winning ad set and compare it with the original.
Refresh worn-out creative before increasing spend.

quote.text: only scale ads that are profitable getting consistent results not showing signs of fatigue
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Handle inbound leads with a simple system
steps: Set an instant reply in Messenger or Instagram to confirm receipt and set expectations.
Track name, contact details, date contacted and lead status in a spreadsheet or CRM.
Write reusable replies for common questions about price, timing and scope.
Review and update the lead tracker regularly.

quote.text: at a bare minimum use a Google sheet you just want to get their name the contact info and the date contacted and the status
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Research competitors’ active ads
steps: Search the Meta Ads Library for competitors.
Review active ads and compare format, headline, hook and image.
Treat ads that appear to have run for months as candidates to study, not guaranteed winners.

quote.text: go to the meta ads library google it search for your competitors sort by active ads scroll through
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test social proof and customer language
steps: Ask customers to record authentic vertical testimonials.
Use real customer wording in ad copy.
Poll or survey an existing audience, then ask willing respondents follow-up questions.
Test a hook organically before paying to distribute a video ad.

quote.text: screenshot their answers and use that exact language in your ad copy now you know you're getting to the heart of the problems
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Validate demand before building
steps: Create a simple landing page for the proposed product.
Run ads to measure clicks or collect email addresses and pre-orders.
If the product cannot be fulfilled, refund pre-orders.

quote.text: sell it before you build it run ads for an idea before you even have the product
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Do not edit a new ad during its learning period unless it is rejected or clearly broken; changes may reset learning.

quote.text: if you change anything major like the budget the creative or the audience you're going to reset the clock
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Traffic campaigns can optimize for clickers rather than buyers or message senders.

quote.text: if you choose traffic as the objective Facebook will show your ad to people who are known clickers not buyers not message senders
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Changing multiple test variables at once makes it impossible to tell which change caused the result.

quote.text: if you change your image your headline your targeting your call to action all at once and your performance improves great what did you do
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Scaling too quickly can disrupt a campaign; the host recommends gradual increases or duplicating the ad set.

quote.text: don't double your budget overnight people do this all the time that kills the learning phase
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Slow lead response, unclear next steps and robotic replies can prevent message leads from turning into bookings.

quote.text: maybe you're too slow to reply or maybe your prices are too high maybe you sound like a robot in your replies

lessons.lesson: Align the customer’s problem, the offer and the audience before spending on creative.

quote.text: a clear problem number two a relevant offer and number three it needs to be shown to the right person at the right time
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pick the campaign objective that matches the action you want; otherwise the platform may optimize for the wrong behavior.

quote.text: just pick one that aligns with your goal
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Make the offer concrete by naming the problem, the solution, the timing and the next action.

quote.text: the tighter the offer the better the ad will perform
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use clear, direct language and real proof instead of polished but vague brand copy.

quote.text: you don't need to be cute you need to be clear
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Treat advertising as a measured system: change one variable at a time and use results to guide the next test.

quote.text: run clean tests watch real metrics and optimize with intention scale what works kill what doesn't and do it all over again
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A winning ad only helps if the business can respond quickly and fulfil the resulting demand.

quote.text: scaling is not magic it's math if you can turn $20 into $200 then turn 40 into 400 but only if you can keep up with the demand
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use customer language and authentic customer stories to make ads specific and credible.

quote.text: use that exact language in your ad copy now you know you're getting to the heart of the problems
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Validate demand before investing heavily in a product; provide refunds when a pre-order cannot be fulfilled.

quote.text: sell it before you build it run ads for an idea before you even have the product
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Revenue return on ad spend does not establish profitability unless product costs and overhead are also accounted for.

quote.text: but that doesn't account for your other overhead or cost so you're really losing money
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Automate routine lead acknowledgement and tracking, while using templates to speed up human replies.
